nodes.label: Ethics and regulation
nodes.question: Why is there increasing scrutiny on the practice of depositing SPL?
nodes.answer: There is increasing scrutiny due to the rising costs associated with depositing SPL and the environmental concerns linked to waste management practices in the aluminum industry.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Circular economy energy|Sustainable mining practices for energy metals_qna_001
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What process developed by Rio Tinto is currently industrialized?
nodes.answer: Rio Tinto has developed the low-caustic leaching and liming process (LCL&L), which is industrialized today.
nodes.subtopic: Sustainable mining practices for energy metals

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Circular economy energy|Sustainable mining practices for energy metals_qna_002
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What challenges are associated with the use of plant biomass in rare earth mining site remediation?
nodes.answer: The challenge concerns how to use secondary resources such as plant biomass following the extraction of rare earth elements (REEs).
nodes.subtopic: Sustainable mining practices for energy metals

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Circular economy energy|Sustainable mining practices for energy metals_qna_003
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: How do the rare earth elements (REEs) in Dicranopteris pedata contribute during the carbonisation process?
nodes.answer: The REEs enriched in Dicranopteris pedata contribute to the formation of rare earth oxides and oxygen vacancies, enhancing the Pb removal ability of REEs/C.
nodes.subtopic: Sustainable mining practices for energy metals

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Circular economy energy|Sustainable mining practices for energy metals_qna_004
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: Did the REEs contained in REEs/C cause any leaching during lead removal?
nodes.answer: No, the REEs contained in the material did not cause a leaching phenomenon during Pb removal.
nodes.subtopic: Sustainable mining practices for energy metals

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Circular economy energy|Sustainable mining practices for energy metals_qna_005
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: What are the two critical questions that need to be resolved regarding REEs/C?
nodes.answer: The two questions are: (1) what are the differences in chemical composition and surface properties at different calcination temperatures; and (2) can the REEs/C be deployed to remove heavy metals such as Pb(II)?

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Circular economy energy|Sustainable mining practices for energy metals_qna_006
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: Which other metals and minerals might also require direct water consumption in addition to copper?
nodes.answer: Other metals and minerals such as nickel, aluminium, iron, and gold may also require direct water consumption in their production processes.
nodes.subtopic: Sustainable mining practices for energy metals

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Circular economy energy|Sustainable mining practices for energy metals_qna_007
nodes.label: Management
nodes.question: How can sustainable minerals and metals contribute to achieving a low-carbon future, as discussed by Lovacott et al. (2020)?
nodes.answer: According to Lovacott et al. (2020), sustainable minerals and metals can contribute to a low-carbon future by enabling the production of renewable energy technologies such as solar panels, wind turbines, and electric vehicle batteries.

nodes.question: How do European mining companies contribute to sustainable development, as evidenced in their sustainability reports?
nodes.answer: European mining companies demonstrate their contributions to sustainable development through their sustainability reports, highlighting the drivers of sustainability practices within the industry.

nodes.label: Management
nodes.question: How can Russia achieve the objectives set by its 2030 Strategy?
nodes.answer: By combining investments and new mining land processing technologies with the involvement of Chinese, Japanese, and Korean companies in energy partnerships and joint ventures.
